name: Ambiente Sedona, A Landscape Hotel
positioning: Independent, family-operated landscape hotel of elevated glass Atriums on the border of the national forest in Sedona, Arizona
best_for: Travelers who want private rooftop stargazing with a fire pit and daybed
Guests who want a spa and on-site dining with red rock views

facts.text: Set on the border of the national forest, the hotel is a collection of elevated Atriums perched above the natural landscape of Sedona.
Views from the hotel span from the Brins Mesa mountain range to a series of ancient waterways weaving through the property.
The resort's design incorporated the restoration of an ancient waterway, which guests enjoy as a water feature throughout the property.
The hotel is family-operated by Mike Stevenson and his two daughters, Jennifer May and Colleen TeBrake.
Atrium bath amenities are by Byredo, in its Gypsy Water scent.
Atrium stays include breakfast for two each morning at Forty1 Restaurant.
Ambiente does not charge any resort fees.
Lexus guest shuttle vehicles are available for Sedona Airport and local attraction pick-up and drop-off.
Restaurant Forty1 is led by Arizona natives Chef Bri Barker and Beverage Manager Rachelle Connolly, with a local-first philosophy.
Forty1 serves modern American cuisine built around Verde Valley produce, Arizona-raised proteins and seasonal ingredients.
Forty1's patio is a pool-side terrace with outdoor fire pits and panoramic red rock views.
Velvet Spa offers massages, body treatments, facials, couples' rituals, sound journeys, energy work, CBD treatments, soaking baths and IV infusions.

highlights.text: The Atriums are made of floor-to-ceiling, bronze-tinted glass that gives 180-degree views of the surrounding red rocks.
Each Atrium has a rooftop deck with a fire pit and daybed.
Sedona is one of just 20 certified Dark Sky Communities in the world.
Each Atrium has a freestanding, two-person Hinoki tub.
At Velvet Spa, guests choose from six scent blends that are worked into their treatments.

considerations.text: Reiki and cranial treatments can be done on the Atrium rooftop only when weather permits, and at an additional charge.
Creekside Atriums are fully ADA compliant.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing that reflects the hotel's exclusive positioning.
